rules.reason: Importing UI components into services couples server-side logic to browser rendering. This breaks SSR, testability, and separation of concerns.
rules.whatBreaks: Server-side services gain browser-only dependencies. Unit tests for services fail. SSR breaks.
examples: Respect the layer boundary described.

rules.description: Controllers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Direct DB access in controllers bypasses the service layer. This breaks the layered architecture and makes logic untestable.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic leaks into controllers. Database coupling makes refactoring expensive.
examples: Respect the layer boundary described.

rules.description: Route handlers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Routes should delegate to services/controllers, not query the database themselves.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic scattered across route files. Impossible to test in isolation.
examples: Respect the layer boundary described.

rules.description: UI components cannot import server-only modules.
rules.reason: Server-only modules may contain secrets or Node.js-only APIs that crash in the browser.
rules.whatBreaks: Build errors in browser environments. Potential secret exposure.
examples: Respect the layer boundary described.

rules.description: High-impact clusters (Config, Other, Database) must not gain new circular dependencies.
rules.reason: High-impact clusters already coordinate many modules. Adding circular imports makes builds fragile.
rules.whatBreaks: Module resolution fails. Build tools (webpack, esbuild) may hang or produce incorrect output.
examples: Use dependency injection or an event bus to break cycles.

rules.description: Environment secrets must never be hardcoded in source files.
rules.reason: Secrets committed to source are exposed via version control history and repository access.
rules.whatBreaks: Security breach. API keys, database credentials, and tokens compromised.
examples: Found in: .kilo/worktrees/ginger-myrtle/frontend/src/lib/supabase.ts, frontend/src/lib/ai.ts

rules.description: Environment variable files (.env) must never be committed to version control.
rules.reason: .env files contain secrets. Committing them exposes credentials to all repository users.
rules.whatBreaks: All secrets in .env become public. Immediate security incident.
examples: Ensure .env is in .gitignore.
Use a secrets manager for production.

rules.description: Payment processing (PCI-DSS) — all Stripe/payment code requires compliance review.
rules.reason: PCI-DSS requires that all payment card data handling meets security standards. Any change to payment flows must be reviewed.
rules.whatBreaks: PCI compliance violation. Payment processor account suspension. Legal liability.
examples: Always review PCI-related code before merging.
Found in: .kilo/worktrees/ginger-myrtle/frontend/src/components/simplified/ClearNextActions.tsx, .tokencap/constitution/compliance-rules.md

rules.description: HIPAA compliance — protected health information (PHI) handling must remain compliant.
rules.reason: HIPAA requires strict access control, audit logging, and encryption for all PHI. Removing protections is illegal.
rules.whatBreaks: HIPAA violation. Criminal liability. Patient data exposed.
examples: Always review HIPAA-related code before merging.
Found in: .kilo/worktrees/ginger-myrtle/frontend/src/app/not-found.tsx, .kilo/worktrees/ginger-myrtle/frontend/src/app/page.tsx

rules.description: Audit logging must always be written and never removed.
rules.reason: Audit logs provide the immutable record required for compliance, forensic investigation, and regulatory review.
rules.whatBreaks: Compliance audit failures. Inability to investigate security incidents. Regulatory violations.
examples: Always review AUDIT-related code before merging.
